data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'agapē', meaning 'love'. In Christian tradition, Carisia represents the deep and unwavering love of God towards his people. The name Carisia carries the meaning “Beloved” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Carisia usually hope their child will grow to embody beloved and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name signifying God's boundless love and compassion for his children.
data.etymology: Carisia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Beloved.”

in_hebrew.name: קאריסיה
in_hebrew.meaning: קאריסיה - שמה של נערה נוצרייה עם משמעות מיוחדת
in_hebrew.long_meaning: קאריסיה הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו ביוונית ומשמעותו 'שמחה' או 'אושר'. השם קאריסיה נמצא בשימוש בעיקר במסגרת השמות הנוצריים והוא מיועד לבנות. השם מבוסס על המילה היוונית 'χάρις' (חאריס), שפירושה 'חסד' או 'שמחה'. השימוש בשם קאריסיה הוא בעיקר במסגרת המסורת הנוצרית והוא נמצא בשימוש במגוון תרבויות נוצריות.

in_greek.name: Καρισία
in_greek.meaning: Καρισία - χαρά ή ευτυχία για το κορίτσι
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Καρισία προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'χάρις' που σημαίνει 'χάρη' ή 'ευτυχία'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, η λέξη 'χάρις' χρησιμοποιείται για να περιγράψει τη θεία χάρη και αγάπη. Το όνομα Καρισία είναι δημοφιλές στην Ορθόδοξη Εκκλησία και συμβολίζει τη χαρά και την ευτυχία που φέρνει ο Θεός στη ζωή των ανθρώπων.

historical_references.reference: Carisia was a city in ancient Phrygia, now modern Turkey. It was an important Christian center during the Byzantine Empire, and was famed for its magnificent basilicas and monastic communities.
historical_references.context: The Byzantine Empire was the continuation of the Roman Empire in its Eastern provinces during the Middle Ages. It was a major power in Europe and the Mediterranean world, and was characterized by its political instability, religious fervor, and artistic achievements.

historical_references.reference: Carisia was also the name of a region in Roman Dalmatia, now modern Croatia. It was known for its strong Christian tradition, and was the site of several important early Christian basilicas and bishoprics.
historical_references.context: The Early Christian Era was the period of early Christian history during which the religion spread from the Middle East to Europe and Africa. It was characterized by the establishment of the Holy See in Rome, the Councils of Nicaea and Chalcedon, and the consolidation of Christian communities in the Western and Eastern Roman Empires.
